conviction_note: Nothing about the period has been pre-released (Elior put out no Q3 or Q4 revenue release), and the release carries the first FY2026-27 guide, so this is a guidance event. The name moved 22.8% (median absolute) on its last five results days and has a thin float: Derichebourg holds 48%, Cobas 15%. So abs_move is 13. The sign rests only on proxies, set against FY27 consensus that expects EPS almost to double: a second SMIC increase with the first coup de pouce since 2012, energy CPI +24%, a peer whose FY27 guide came in below consensus, and shorts building again. Against those, the loss-making Italian rail contract is reported as transferred out in September. Hence p_up 44 and expected (2*0.44-1)*13 = -1.56, close to the findings sum of -1.2.

already_public.what: H1 2025-26 (to 31 Mar 2026): revenue EUR 3.18bn, organic +1.3%, adjusted EBITA EUR 95m (3.0% margin, 3.9% excluding a EUR 25m loss-to-completion provision on an Italian rail contract), net income EUR 21m, FCF EUR 9m, leverage 3.6x. FY2025-26 guidance cut to organic +1-2% (from 3-4%), adjusted EBITA margin about 3% (from 3.5-3.7%), leverage about 3.5x at end-September (from about 3x); the guide excludes the Italian rail contract
Market reaction to the cut: -26.76% on 2026-05-21, to EUR 2.06. TP Icap said adjusted EBIT excluding the provision was EUR 120m against a EUR 137m consensus
Early repayment of EUR 159m of July 2026 senior notes. EUR 150m tap of the 2030 notes on 2026-02-25, so the 2026 maturity is handled
BNP Paribas Exane downgraded to Neutral from Outperform and cut its target to EUR 2.00 from 3.50. The stock fell about 5-6.7% to about EUR 1.74-1.77
Dividend policy set at FY25: about 30% of group net income

new_in_release.expect: First FY2026-27 guide. Consensus (S&P via stockanalysis) has EPS rising from 0.15 to 0.29 and revenue +3.1%. Lean: below consensus on margin (SMIC, energy, the peer's conservative FY27 guide), with possibly healthy organic growth from contract start-ups (Yvelines colleges from 2026, a La Défense bank HQ). Direction uncertain, lean negative
FY26 should land inside the cut guide (organic 1-2%, margin about 3%). The H2 numbers are new, because there was no Q3/Q4 revenue release. Expect roughly in line
FY FCF and leverage against the 3.5x guide. H1 FCF was only EUR 9m because of a billing delay and working capital. Unknown, with negative risk
About 30% payout on lower net income, so a smaller dividend than FY25 or none. Unknown
Italian rail contract: exit or transfer, any release of or addition to the EUR 25m provision, and any disposal result. Lean mildly positive, because it clears an overhang

findings.finding: France's minimum wage rises another 1.6% on 2026-12-01, the first government 'coup de pouce' since 2012 (announced 2026-11-09), on top of the automatic +2.41% of 2026-06-01. The bottom pay grades of 64 branches, propreté (cleaning) and hôtellerie-restauration among them, now fall below the SMIC. Employer contribution relief is to be made conditional on compliant grids. This is a direct FY27 labour-cost headwind for Elior France (contract catering) and Multiservices (cleaning), landing on the first FY27 guide against consensus that expects EPS almost to double.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide decides this stock. -24.3% on the prudent outlook of Nov 2024, +6.8% on the FY26 guide of Nov 2025, -26.8% on the cut of May 2026 (baseline history plus ilsole24ore).
findings.original_quote: Le SMIC augmente de 1,6% au 1er décembre 2026, atteignant 1 502 euros nets mensuels, dans une décision qui combine évolution automatique et premier coup de pouce gouvernemental depuis 2012. [...] L'hôtellerie-restauration, le commerce de détail, les services à la personne et la propreté figurent parmi les secteurs concernés. (Translation: the SMIC rises 1.6% on 1 December 2026 to EUR 1,502 net a month, combining the automatic revaluation with the first government top-up since 2012; hotels and restaurants, retail, personal services and cleaning are among the sectors affected.)
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has risen from 1.93 to 1.96 since the 2026-11-09 announcement and run up 10% in 20 days. Sell-side targets were last moved on 2026-10-19, before the announcement. If the market had marked FY27 down for it, FY27 EPS consensus would not still sit at about 2x FY26. This is macro-to-company transmission: Elior has not quantified it, and indexation clauses pass part of it on with a lag.
findings.independence: Energy CPI +24.1% y/y in October, accelerating for a fourth month (INSEE, https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/9107975), is a separate cost pressure. The 2026-06-01 automatic +2.41% is confirmed separately (https://bourseinside.fr/economie/smic-cette-hausse-de-24-au-1er-juin-2026-cache-un-changement-cle-sur-votre-fiche-de-paie-et-vos-aides-attention/).

findings.finding: Sodexo, Elior's closest French peer, guided FY2027 on 2026-10-23 to organic +2-3% with the margin flat at 3.4%. Citi said the guide implies an operating margin about 8% below consensus; Barclays called FY27 growth and margin below consensus. Sodexo Europe grew organic +2.1% in FY26, with a stronger-than-expected Q4. Read-through: European contract caterers are guiding FY27 conservatively into investment and cost inflation, while Elior's FY27 consensus assumes a sharp margin recovery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same guide line as above: -24.3% (Nov 2024 prudent guide), +6.8% (Nov 2025), -26.8% (May 2026 cut).
findings.original_quote: Citi note que les prévisions du groupe pour 2027 impliquent une marge opérationnelle inférieure de 8% au consensus [...] "Les prévisions pour l'exercice 2027 pourraient s'avérer décevantes, la croissance en données comparables et les marges s'inscrivant tous deux en deçà du consensus", abonde Barclays. (Translation: Citi notes the 2027 guide implies an operating margin 8% below consensus; Barclays adds that the FY27 guide could disappoint, with like-for-like growth and margins both below consensus.)
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer proxy. Elior's consensus was not visibly cut after Sodexo: the S&P average still shows FY27 EPS at 0.29, almost 2x FY26. The peer's positive European Q4 volume partly offsets the read, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Sodexo FY26 detail (Europe +2.1%, Q4 above expectations, FY27 margin flat) from a separate outlet: https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/sodexo-annonce-une-croissance-organique-de-2-0-en-2026-et-confirme-ses-objectif_704818 . It is the same underlying release, so it corroborates rather than adds an independent signal.

findings.finding: Il Giorno reported on 2026-07-04 that Elior's Italian 'ramo treni', the Trenitalia high-speed and long-distance onboard catering contract (about 2,000 staff), is being transferred to a newco, Onboard Services SpA, with the handover planned for September 2026. That is the contract behind the pricing dispute and the EUR 25m loss-to-completion provision. The FY release should show Elior exiting the loss-making contract (scope effect, possible provision release or disposal result), which removes the overhang from FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The provision on this contract helped drive the -26.8% of 2026-05-21. Its exit has never been priced on a results day.
findings.original_quote: Il "ramo treni" della multinazionale Elior, a cui Trenitalia ha appaltato il servizio di ristorazione e assistenza ai clienti sull'alta velocità e sulle tratte a lunga percorrenza, verrà trasferito infatti alla nuova società Onboard Services Spa, che per effetto della clausola sociale da settembre dovrà assorbire tutti i dipendenti (Translation: Elior's train branch, which Trenitalia contracted for catering and passenger assistance on high-speed and long-distance routes, will be transferred to the new company Onboard Services SpA, which from September must take on all employees under the social clause.)
findings.why_not_priced: Elior has issued no press release on it (the company press list from June to November 2026 has none). It appears only in Italian regional and union press; no French or English financial outlet covered it. The May guide already excluded the contract, so the operating effect is small and the value is mostly in removing the dispute risk. It is a one-off with only a partial path to the FY27 margin, so it is sized as a fraction. Not confirmed in a primary document.
findings.independence: The union meeting records of 8 and 25 June are cited inside the same article, so there is no separately sourced confirmation. The H1 provision and dispute are from a different source: https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/elior-revise-a-la-baisse-ses-objectifs-annuels-evoquant-le-deploiement-decale-d_697140

findings.finding: Disclosed net shorts are building into the print. The aggregate rose from 1.20-1.29% to 1.69% as a third seller crossed 0.5% on the 2026-11-16 position date, after the register had fallen from about 2.47% in October.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed link on this name between register moves and the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The register is public and the baseline's priced lean already carries it (short_building -0.8), so this is mostly priced and sized near zero. At about 4.6% of free float it is not crowded enough to be squeeze fuel.
findings.independence: Retail forum data shows short-sale volume down 31% over a week and 47% over a month (https://www.abcbourse.com/forums/msg1114411_elior-chute-de-pres-de-5-en-bourse-apres-une-degradation-de-bnp-pari). That is volume, not position, and it points the other way.

findings.finding: Cobas Asset Management crossed 15% of Elior on 2026-06-24 (38,426,298 shares, 15.15%), after 10% on 2026-04-01, with a passive intent declaration. With Derichebourg at about 48%, the free float is about 37% and daily turnover about $0.58m, which widens the reaction whichever way it goes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since the float tightened the stock has moved -26.8% on one results day (May 2026). The BFM article notes that limited free float makes Elior react strongly to publications.

findings.finding: French input-cost inflation in Elior's H2 (Jul-Sep) and into FY27 is split. Food CPI eased to 1.4% in September and 1.2% in October, less than the 'retour de l'inflation' Elior flagged in May. Energy CPI accelerated for a fourth month to +24.1% y/y (fuel and kitchens). Net effect on H2 margin is about neutral.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Inflation was one of the three causes named for the May 2026 cut (-26.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public macro series and the two components offset, so it is sized at 0. Filed because it bears on the H2 margin.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly negative, in line with the priced lean (-0.30) and the shorts building, and against the +10.2% 20-day run-up, which in turn sits inside a -8.1% 60-day move and a -27% gap since May. None of it is a company-level number the market has not seen, so p_up stays near 50.
language_note: The French sources carried the SMIC detail: the 2026-12-01 +1.6% with the first coup de pouce since 2012, the cleaning and catering branch grids falling below the minimum, and relief made conditional on compliant grids. No English source on Elior connects any of this
The French AMF filings carried Cobas's 15.15% crossing (24 June 2026) and its passive intent declaration, which sets the free float at about 37%

The French wire copy (AOF via ABC Bourse) carried the detail that the FY26 guide excludes the Italian rail contract and the 'confortablement en deçà des covenants à 4,5' line. The English Il Sole copy had the headline numbers only
The Italian rail contract transfer to Onboard Services SpA came from Italian regional press (Il Giorno), not from French or English sources
The French broker coverage (BFM, ABC Bourse) carried the BNP Exane downgrade with its EUR 2.00 target; the English sources carried only undated downgrades
lessons_applied: 'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it': SMIC finding cut from -1.2 to -1.0
'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with': the shorts-building finding cut from -0.5 to -0.2, because the baseline lean already carries it

p_up moved from 43 to 44 as a result. abs_move_pct kept at 13 under 'the move is in the guide' (first FY27 guide) and 'reaction history moves p_up, not abs_move'. A one-off is sized at a fraction, so the Italy finding stays at +0.5
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': cash_flow added to new_in_release as a downside risk, unsized because there is no new source
